summary.name: Paper Cutout Illustration (Printmaking and Craft Materials; explicit provenance).
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: objects are built from clearly cut paper shapes with thin visible edges, soft contact shadows and stacked sheet layers. Paper colors and material types are limited. Flat cutouts keep a matte, handmade look without implying physical paper texture.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: source guidance pairs this style with narrative openers, brand origin stories, calm scene transitions, and explainers showing a few verified comparisons or process steps. Inferred: craft-based or handmade educational topics. Quantified content should use data-derived geometry, since freehand cut shapes may not carry exact values.
summary.limitations: Cut shapes do not supply physical paper texture or 3D curl. The procedural curl is artistic deformation, not a paper physics solver, and a 3D renderer is needed only when depth or curling is required. Avoid curl on data marks, torn edges that change apparent value, and more than three chart categories. Source review covered only one sampled frame per second for seconds 1–8 of two sources; continuous motion, sub-second timing and audio were not verified.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent. The cream #F2EAD8 is an illustrative swatch, not a required canvas, and its tint should follow the subject and lighting. Suggested tokens are foreground #304849, accent_1 #C17F63 and accent_2 #829776. No approved exact colors were supplied. Foreground on background measures 8.161:1; accents at about 3.0–3.1:1 are decorative only. Gradients are disabled. Keep matte paper fills, a limited color-family count, dark ink type and sparse accents.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: pieces move on believable joints by sliding, rotating and folding, using deliberate pose changes that avoid intersections and conflicting shadow directions. Video is driven by composition time. Interactive delivery may use capped pointer or scroll parallax on whole planes, disabled under reduced motion. Sharp cuts and reading holds are preserved; easing is not required on every move.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the style; source samples verified no audio. Suggested, not required: optional background music, voiceover, restrained paper-sound accents, ambience or silence, chosen from topic, mood and cadence. No fixed genre or tempo applies. Honor any explicit user audio, avoid competing with narration, and use measured audio timing before any beat-synchronized cuts.
summary.assetRequirements: Prepared paper contours with slightly irregular edges, contact-shadow layers, defined pivots and parent-child joints, and transparent layered PNG or SVG at consistent dimensions. Fonts and assets must load before rendering. Numbered frames are optional. No photographs or brand marks are required, and copy must not be invented. Missing supplied assets must be reported, not silently replaced.
summary.combinations: Style-101 adds depth layering and one shared camera pan across paper planes, with one light direction and artwork bled past the crop. Style-097 adds data-driven cut strips limited to accent_1, accent_2 and foreground. Motion-037 and 038 are optional when assets support rotating letters or a paper punctuation crop. Motion-012 and 015 fit chaptered narratives; motion-006 and 009 need character or creature assets.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit: HyperFrames is the default pipeline for scene assembly, timing, validation and export; Remotion is a fallback only for a verified limitation. SVG is the primary style renderer, with optional PixiJS or Paper.js for layered or vector geometry. GSAP drives a paused, seekable motion timeline with one owner per animated property. chroma-js checks contrast. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks against decoded frames.
